OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '^.*\S.*$'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '^.*\S.*$'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is
            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits;
            the result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The stored and
            returned value is that E.164 string, e.g. '0412 345 678' becomes
            '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation"
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2024-01-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag used on create. When an existing owner already has
            the same last name and the same address (compared case-insensitively
            with collapsed whitespace), the create is rejected with 409 unless
            this flag is set to true, which acknowledges the two owners share a
            household and allows the create to proceed.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          default: false
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName

## Summary

I implemented address normalization for owner creation in the Spring Boot PetClinic REST app.

**Change made** — `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java`:

Added a `normalizeAddress` method (wired into the create-path `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` mapping via `@Mapping(... qualifiedByName = "normalizeAddress")`), following the existing `normalizeTelephone`/`normalizeEmail` idiom. It:
- trims and collapses runs of whitespace to a single space,
- upper-cases the result,
- expands common street abbreviations (`ST`→`STREET`, `RD`→`ROAD`, `AVE`→`AVENUE`) as whole tokens via a small lookup map.

**How the spec requirements are satisfied:**
- *Store and return the normalized address* — normalization happens in the create mapper, so the persisted `Owner.address` and the value returned by `toOwnerDto` are both normalized (e.g. `"  12  main  st "` → `"12 MAIN STREET"`, `"7 elm ave"` → `"7 ELM AVENUE"`).
- *Reject blank after normalization* — the generated DTO's `@Pattern("^.*\S.*$")` already rejects any address lacking a non-whitespace character, which is exactly "blank after trim/collapse"; since none of the normalization steps can turn non-whitespace into blank, a whitespace-only address (`"   "`) is correctly rejected with 400.
- *Comparisons use the normalized form* — because every created owner's address is normalized at the mapper before it reaches `ClinicServiceImpl`, both household duplicate detection (`isHouseholdInUse`) and the shared household id (`assignHousehold`/`generateHouseholdId`) already operate on the normalized address with no further change needed; their `normalizeHouseholdValue` case-folding sits consistently on top.

Update (`updateOwner`) intentionally stays untouched — the spec scopes normalization to owner *creation*, and that path uses setters rather than the create mapper.

One thing worth flagging: the "blank after normalization" rejection is handled by the pre-existing DTO `@Pattern` on the raw input rather than a check on the post-normalization string. These are behaviorally equivalent here (no non-blank input can normalize to blank), so I avoided adding an unreachable guard — but if you'd prefer the required-field check to literally run against the normalized value, I can move it into the controller/service instead.
